question: How much is a federal backbencher paid?

sentences.text: A federal backbencher, a senator or member with no other post, is paid a base salary of $239,270 a year.
That is the salary entitlement the Remuneration Tribunal sets, not a payslip: the electorate allowance ($39,700 to $57,100 a year), expenses and superannuation are not included.

meta.method: For each day a person sat in the federal parliament: the parliamentary base salary then in force, plus the additional salary of the post they then held, as a percentage of that base. A Minister is paid the one ministerial rate that applies. Other office holders are paid the sum of the percentages of their offices, rounded up to the next $10; a shadow minister is paid a flat rate instead. Yearly figures add those days across a financial year. Nothing is adjusted for inflation.

not_covered.text: Committee chairs and deputy chairs are paid a further 3% to 16% that is not counted, because the Parliamentary Handbook gives no dates for who chaired what.
A shadow minister is paid a loading only if named in the Opposition Leader’s notice to the Clerks, which is capped and not published; Opax assumes every listed shadow minister is named.

meta.measure: Total remuneration: the Remuneration Tribunal's measure of the total cost to the employer of salary, allowances, benefits and the employer superannuation contribution, per year.
notes: Every amount is total remuneration per year, which includes the employer superannuation contribution and benefits; a parliamentarian's salary (pay.json) does not include superannuation.
Secretaries at levels 3 and 4 are assigned to a pay point by the Secretary of the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, so their rate is shown as the level's range.
A Principal Executive Office band is a range: the employing body sets the holder's pay within it, and band E has no upper limit.
Actual pay, including any performance pay and leave paid out, is reported in each body's annual report.
not_covered: Which office sits in which Principal Executive Office band (set by ministerial declaration, not in the determination).
Judges and judicial offices, the Governor-General, and bodies that set their own executive pay outside the Tribunal (such as the Reserve Bank).
Who holds each office, except where the determination itself names the holder.
